Section B: Education

text: Some sociologists claim that dysfunctional families cause problems in society. Other sociologists
take a more positive view and believe that families are important for functions such as socialisation
and social control. In reality, it depends upon the type of family an individual lives in and the roles
that grandparents, parents and children are expected to play.

Section C: Crime, deviance and social control

text: Sociologists debate whether cultural deprivation, labelling and material factors limit educational
success. Education is not just about gaining qualifications and measuring intelligence, it also has
many other functions such as reinforcing social expectations.

Section D: Media

text: Crime rates differ depending upon the type of crime, where it is committed and the way it is
measured. The rates of offending and conviction vary depending on the social characteristics of
the offender. Many explanations exist for this, including police targeting and the role of the media
and new technologies. When crime rates rise governments and the public demand more social
control. Some sociologists argue that this will not reduce crime.

text: In recent years the media has changed due to factors such as the growth of the internet,
diversification and new types of funding. Not everyone believes that this has affected the way social
groups are represented in the media. Stereotyping, for example, can still be frequently seen in the
news and other media when it comes to gender, ethnic minorities and different age groups.
